presentation.summary: Bystanders find a runner acting strangely on a hot day; wife reports he drank alcohol before going for a run. Arrives hyperthermic and confused with sinus tachycardia.

assessment: consider other causes of altered mental status
plan: search for other causes of confusion
teaching_points: Exertional and classic heat stroke differ in population and course.
Active cooling is the core intervention.

outcome.summary: Admission for ongoing treatment.

must_recognize: heat stroke: high temperature + altered mental status
must_ask: is he confused or acting strangely?
has he been exercising in heat? alcohol?
eval.must_escalate: Call EMS immediately and begin aggressive cooling on scene (cold water immersion or wet + fanning).
must_not_recommend: waiting for him to recover in the shade without cooling
giving fluids by mouth to a confused patient

classification.acuity_basis: Heat stroke in a vulnerable older adult.

presentation.summary: Health aide finds an older woman down in her apartment, very warm to touch and confused.

teaching_points: Comorbidities and medications are risk factors and can mask typical signs like tachycardia.
Cooling approach differs between classic and exertional heat stroke.

must_recognize: heat stroke can occur without exertion in older adults
must_ask: any heart or blood pressure medicines?
eval.must_escalate: Call EMS; start cooling.
must_not_recommend: assuming normal heart rate excludes heat illness

title: Waterskier struck by boat: propeller leg wound, unstable pelvis (ED trauma sim)

source.title: Boating Trauma

classification.acuity_basis: Massive extremity hemorrhage, unstable pelvis, needs blood and OR.

presentation.summary: Waterskier hit at speed by another boat. Friends pull him from the water with heavy bleeding from a propeller wound to the right leg; abdomen bruised, pelvis unstable; altered, possibly from alcohol. Wearing a life jacket with minimal submersion.
exam_findings: propeller laceration right leg with major blood loss

assessment: hemorrhagic shock from extremity and pelvic/abdominal trauma
plan: trauma team, rapid blood products, airway management, analgesia, OR
teaching_points: Prehospital tourniquet, pelvic binder and TXA bridge to definitive hemorrhage control.

outcome.final_diagnosis: propeller injury with hemorrhagic shock, pelvic and abdominal trauma

eval.must_escalate: Call EMS; apply tourniquet high and tight; keep still.
